The baseline#

This page explains the baseline run takes before the first hop. Next: A smoke test for WSU apps.

Before the first hop, run runs the app's own tests (or the built-in php -l syntax check when the app has no tests) on the PHP the app is on now, in the same booster-target:<php> image the gate uses. The point is to tell "Booster broke it" from "it was already broken": a red baseline means the suite was red before any change, so a later red gate is not proof of a bad hop. The baseline is recorded in the report (passed, failed or skipped, with the exit code and the last 20 lines of output).

  • A red baseline stops the run before the first hop, with a non-zero exit. --allow-failing-baseline lets it go on; each later gate failure is then labeled "the baseline was already failing" in the text and JSON output.
  • --skip-gate and --dry-run skip the baseline (reported as skipped), so a dry run never starts Docker.
  • A Mix app's public/mix-manifest.json is a build artifact, not committed source: a fresh clone has no manifest, so the suite can be red before any hop. Build the assets before the baseline (the app's usual npm ci && npm run build), or pass --allow-failing-baseline knowing why.
  • When the app has no tests of its own, the baseline and every gate run a built-in check instead: every PHP file outside vendor/ and node_modules/ must still parse on the target PHP (php -l). That proves the code loads on the new PHP, not that it works: click through the app before you ship. Pass --test-command to run something else, or add a smoke test (A smoke test for WSU apps) to get the real gate back.
